title.zh: 卷365 列傳一百五十二 觉罗宝兴 宗室敬徴 宗室禧恩 陈官俊 卓秉恬
title.en: Volume 365 Biographies 152: Jue Luo Bao Xing, Zong Shijingzheng, Zong Shixien, Chen Guanjun, Zhuo Bingtian
title.raw: 卷365 列傳一百五十二 觉罗宝兴 宗室敬徴 宗室禧恩 陈官俊 卓秉恬

sentences.zh: 列傳一百五十二

translations.literal: Biographies 152
translations.idiomatic: Biography 152

sentences.zh: 覺羅寶興宗室敬徵宗室禧恩陳官俊卓秉恬

translations.literal: Jueluo Baoxing, Imperial clansman Jingzheng, Imperial clansman Xi'en, Chen Guanjun, Zhuo Bingtian
translations.idiomatic: Jueluo Baoxing, the imperial clansmen Jingzheng and Xi'en, Chen Guanjun, and Zhuo Bingtian

sentences.zh: 覺羅寶興，字獻山，隸鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: Jueluo Baoxing, style name Xianshan, was registered in the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Jueluo Baoxing (style name Xianshan) belonged to the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 15 he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in Jiaqing 15 (1810), entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷少詹事，入直上書房。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to vice chamberlain and entered permanent service in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to vice chamberlain of the Hanlin Academy and was assigned to the Upper Study on standing duty.

sentences.zh: 十八年，仁宗幸熱河，林清逆黨突入禁城，寶興散直，至東華門與賊遇，急入告警。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Jiaqing Emperor was at Rehe; Lin Qing's rebel faction burst into the Forbidden City. Baoxing was off duty; reaching the East Flowery Gate he met the rebels and rushed in to raise the alarm.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 18 (1813), while the Jiaqing Emperor was at Rehe, Lin Qing's rebels broke into the Forbidden City. Baoxing was between shifts; at the East Flowery Gate he ran into the assailants and dashed inside to sound the alarm.

sentences.zh: 宣宗方在上書房，聞警戒備，賊不得逞。

translations.literal: The Daoguang Emperor was then in the Upper Study; hearing the alarm, preparations were made and the rebels could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The future Daoguang Emperor was in the Upper Study; once the warning spread, the palace was put on guard and the rebels were thwarted.

sentences.zh: 上還京，擢寶興內閣學士。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, Baoxing was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Beijing, Baoxing was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 19 (1814) he was made vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以事忤旨，詔斥寶興不學，降大理寺卿，罷直書房。

translations.literal: For an affair that offended the imperial will, an edict rebuked Baoxing as unlearned, demoted him to chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and dismissed him from Upper Study duty.
translations.idiomatic: He later offended the throne on another matter; an edict called him unlearned, demoted him to president of the Court of Judicial Review, and stripped him of Upper Study duty.

sentences.zh: 复坐部刊科場條例誤「高宗」為「高祖」，降二級調用。

translations.literal: He was punished again because his ministry's printed examination regulations mistakenly gave 'Gaozu' for 'Gaozong'; he was demoted two ranks and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: He was penalized again when regulations his ministry published for the civil service examinations named 'Gaozu' instead of 'Gaozong'; he dropped two ranks and was reassigned.

sentences.zh: 尋予三等侍衛，充吐魯番領隊大臣。

translations.literal: Soon he was given third-class imperial bodyguard and appointed leading officer for Turpan.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he received the rank of third-class imperial bodyguard and was sent as the Turpan expedition commissioner.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，召為大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: In Daoguang 2 he was recalled as vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 (1822) he was recalled to serve as vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 復因事降通政司參議，歷左副都御史、兵部侍郎，出為泰宁鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was again demoted for an affair to secretary of the Office of Transmission, and served successively as Left Vice Censor-in-chief and vice minister of War; he went out as commanding general of Taining garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After another demotion he became a secretary in the Office of Transmission, then Left Vice Censor-in-chief and vice minister of War, before leaving the capital as commanding general of Taining.

sentences.zh: 八年，授理籓院侍郎，調兵部。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed vice president of the Lifan Court and transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 8 (1828) he was made vice president of the Lifan Court, then transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 迭命偕戶部尚書王鼎察治長蘆、兩淮鹽務，籌議整頓，詳王鼎傳。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly ordered together with Minister of Revenue Wang Ding to investigate the Changlu and Lianghuai salt administrations and plan reforms; details are in the biography of Wang Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly ordered, together with Wang Ding of the Ministry of Revenue, to investigate salt affairs at Changlu and the Huai region and propose reforms; see Wang Ding's biography.

sentences.zh: 十年，出為吉林將軍，疏言：「松花江西岸、輝發河北岸舊例封禁，其餘閒曠山場均設卡倫，惟許兵丁打捕牲畜，以備貢品。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he went out as General of Jilin. In a memorial he said: 'West of the Songhua River and north of the Huifa River are tracts closed by former regulations; elsewhere idle mountain land all had guard posts, and only soldiers were permitted to hunt livestock for tribute items.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 10 (1830) he was posted General of Jilin. He memorialized: "Lands west of the Songhua and north of the Huifa had long been under closure edicts, while other vacant hills were patrolled by guard posts and only garrison troops might hunt for tribute game.

sentences.zh: 民人無照，私出挖蓡斫木者，查拏治罪。」

translations.literal: Commoners without permits who privately went out to dig ginseng or cut timber were to be seized and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone without a license who ventured out to dig ginseng or harvest timber was to be arrested and punished."

sentences.zh: 又言：「伯都訥珠爾山荒田先後開墾五千二百六十二晌，其租息請自道光十五年為始，以其半分賞兵丁，半存備報修工程。

translations.literal: He also said: 'At Boduna Zhuer Mountain, waste land opened in succession totaled 5,262 shang; please let rent begin from Daoguang 15, half to reward soldiers and half reserved for engineering repairs reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked: "Rents from 5,262 shang of reclaimed wasteland at Boduna Zhuer Mountain should begin in Daoguang 15 (1835), with half disbursed to the troops and half banked for maintenance projects.

sentences.zh: 此外尚有可墾荒地五萬六千餘晌，作為官荒，將來奏請招佃徵租。

translations.literal: Beyond this there was still reclaimable waste land of more than 56,000 shang, to be treated as government waste land and later memorialized for tenant recruitment and rent levies.
translations.idiomatic: Another 56,000-odd shang of reclaimable land should be held as official wasteland until the court could approve tenant settlement and taxation.

sentences.zh: 烏拉涼水泉已墾七萬三千九百餘晌，請撥二道河東二萬晌，以七成給烏拉總管衙門，三成給協領衙門，資為津貼。

translations.literal: At Wula Liangshui Spring 73,900-odd shang had been opened; please allocate 20,000 shang east of the Second River, seventy percent to the Wula commandant's yamen and thirty percent to the assistant commandant's yamen, as allowances.
translations.idiomatic: At Wula's Liangshui Spring some 73,900 shang were already under cultivation; he proposed setting aside 20,000 shang east of the Second River—seventy percent to the Wula commandant and thirty percent to the assistant commandant—as stipends.

sentences.zh: 餘未墾地五萬三千餘晌，亦作官荒。」

translations.literal: The remaining unopened land of more than 53,000 shang was likewise to be government waste land.'
translations.idiomatic: The remaining 53,000-plus shang not yet opened would likewise remain official wasteland."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: The court approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved everything.

sentences.zh: 調盛京，又調成都。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Shengjing, then to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred first to Shengjing, then to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 十七年，署四川總督，逾年實授。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he served as acting governor-general of Sichuan and received substantive appointment the following year.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 17 (1837) he acted as governor-general of Sichuan and received the full appointment a year later.

sentences.zh: 時馬邊、越巂邊外夷匪數出為患。

translations.literal: At the time outside Ma Bian and Yuexi, non-Han bandits frequently raided.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Ma Bian and Yuexi frontiers, Yi and other tribesmen were raiding repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 十九年，疏言：「禦邊之策，不外剿、撫、防三者，撫之之道，在施於平時，斷無失利之後轉而就撫之理。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he memorialized: 'Border policy consists of nothing beyond suppression, pacification, and defense; pacification must be applied in peacetime—there is no reason to turn to pacification only after defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 19 (1839) he argued in a memorial: "Frontier policy rests on suppression, conciliation, and defense, but conciliation works only in quiet times—not as a fallback after military failure.

sentences.zh: 比來勞師糜餉，迄無成功。

translations.literal: Recently troops have been exhausted and funds wasted, yet success has never been achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns had drained men and money without result.

sentences.zh: 為今計者，以修邊防為急務，陳防邊五事：一、增兵額，請於馬邊增兵千二百，雷波、普安、安阜、越巂、寧越各增兵八百，瓘邊、屏山各增兵四百；

translations.literal: For the present plan, strengthening border defense is the urgent task. He set forth five measures for border defense: first, increase troop quotas—request 1,200 more at Ma Bian, 800 each at Leibo, Pu'an, Anfu, Yuexi, and Ningyue, and 400 each at Huanbian and Pingshan;
translations.idiomatic: His immediate proposal was to fortify the frontier. He listed five measures: first, raise troop quotas—1,200 more at Ma Bian, 800 each at Leibo, Pu'an, Anfu, Yuexi, and Ningyue, and 400 each at Huanbian and Pingshan;

sentences.zh: 一、改營製，請以綏定協副將移駐馬邊廳城，游擊、都司以下各增設移駐有差；

translations.literal: second, reform the garrison system—request that the Suiding brigade deputy commander move his headquarters to Ma Bian prefectural city, with additions and relocations of brigade commanders, battalion commanders, and lower ranks as appropriate;
translations.idiomatic: second, reorganize the garrison layout—move the Suiding brigade deputy commander to Ma Bian city and add or redeploy brigade, battalion, and company officers as needed;

sentences.zh: 一、築碉堡，飭各廳縣因地制宜，多修堡寨，責令各集團練，官給抬砲，督率教演，擇要隘築砲台，增設大砲；

translations.literal: third, build forts and stockades—instruct each prefecture and county to suit local conditions, build many fortified hamlets, charge each militia corps to drill, supply swivel guns from the government, supervise training, choose strategic passes for batteries, and add heavy cannon;
translations.idiomatic: third, build forts and stockades—each subprefecture and county should adapt to terrain, multiply fortified villages, drill local militia, issue swivel guns, supervise training, erect batteries at key passes, and add heavy artillery;

sentences.zh: 一、定期巡閱，歲春夏之交，建昌道赴越巂、瓘邊，永寧道赴馬邊、雷波、屏山，週曆巡閱各一次，秋冬責成提督與建昌總兵分赴巡行察勘邊隘；

translations.literal: fourth, schedule regular inspections—between spring and summer each year the Jianchang circuit intendant should tour Yuexi and Huanbian, the Yongning circuit intendant Ma Bian, Leibo, and Pingshan, each making one full round; in autumn and winter the provincial commander-in-chief and Jianchang regional commander should divide duties to patrol and survey border passes;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, institute regular inspections—in late spring the Jianchang intendant would tour Yuexi and Huanbian, the Yongning intendant Ma Bian, Leibo, and Pingshan, each once a year; in autumn the provincial commander and Jianchang regional commander would split patrols to survey the passes;

sentences.zh: 一、優獎邊吏，馬邊、越巂兩廳同知，請三年俸滿，以題調選缺知府升補。」

translations.literal: fifth, reward frontier officials—the subprefects of Ma Bian and Yuexi, upon completing three years' tenure, should be promoted by special selection to vacant prefect posts.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, reward frontier officials—after three years' service the subprefects of Ma Bian and Yuexi should be elevated by special selection to prefectural posts."

sentences.zh: 疏下議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent down for deliberation and carried out.

sentences.zh: 言官論奏四川提督應如湖南例，半年駐越巂等處。

translations.literal: Censorial officials memorialized that the Sichuan provincial commander-in-chief, following the Hunan precedent, should spend half the year stationed at Yuexi and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists argued that the Sichuan commander-in-chief, like his Hunan counterpart, should spend half the year on the Yuexi frontier.

sentences.zh: 寶興議：「馬邊、越巂相距遼遠，請於春秋夷匪出沒之時，提督往駐馬邊、瓘邊、雷波三廳，建昌總兵往駐越巂、寧越。」

translations.literal: Baoxing argued: 'Ma Bian and Yuexi are far apart; please have the commander-in-chief station in spring and autumn, when tribal bandits appear, at the three subprefectures of Ma Bian, Huanbian, and Leibo, and the Jianchang regional commander at Yuexi and Ningyue.'
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing countered: "Ma Bian and Yuexi were too far apart: in spring and autumn, when raiders were active, the commander-in-chief should camp at Ma Bian, Huanbian, and Leibo, while the Jianchang regional commander held Yuexi and Ningyue."

sentences.zh: 又言：「越巂邊防以大路為重，麥子營、利濟站均應增駐弁兵，乾溝諸汛應酌量移撤，分設於馬日槓諸處。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Yuexi border defense hinges on the main road; Maiziying and Lijizhan both need added garrison troops; the posts at Qiangou should be judiciously withdrawn and redeployed to Marigang and other points.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged: "Strengthening the main road through Yuexi is vital—more troops at Maiziying and Lijizhan, and shifting detachments from Qiangou to Marigang and similar posts.

sentences.zh: 越巂、寧越兩營相距頗遠，聲勢不能相及。

translations.literal: The Yuexi and Ningyue battalions were quite far apart and could not support each other.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuexi and Ningyue garrisons lay too far apart to lend each other mutual support.

sentences.zh: 前請以建昌左營游擊移駐大菩薩地，遠在寧越之東，而越巂營參將復與游擊不相統屬。

translations.literal: Previously he had requested that the Jianchang Left Battalion brigade commander move to Dapusa, far east of Ningyue, while the Yuexi Battalion colonel was not in the brigade commander's chain of command.
translations.idiomatic: An earlier plan to move the Jianchang Left Battalion brigade commander to Dapusa—far east of Ningyue—left the Yuexi colonel outside his command.

sentences.zh: 請越巂、寧越適中之界牌樓，以建昌鎮右營都司移駐，專管麥子營、利濟站兩汛。」

translations.literal: He requested that at Jiepailou, midway between Yuexi and Ningyue, the Jianchang Right Battalion battalion commander be moved to take exclusive charge of the two posts at Maiziying and Lijizhan.'
translations.idiomatic: He proposed stationing the Jianchang Right Battalion commander at Jiepailou, midway between Yuexi and Ningyue, to command Maiziying and Lijizhan directly."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: The court approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved everything.

sentences.zh: 先是寶興以馬邊諸廳縣增設防兵，籌議邊防經費，請按糧津貼，計可徵銀百萬兩，以三十萬為初設防兵之需。

translations.literal: Earlier Baoxing, because Ma Bian and other subprefectures and counties were adding frontier troops, planned border defense funds and requested a grain surcharge, calculating that one million taels of silver could be levied, with three hundred thousand for initial troop establishment.
translations.idiomatic: To pay for new garrisons along the Ma Bian line, Baoxing had proposed a grain surcharge expected to yield one million taels—three hundred thousand for startup costs.

sentences.zh: 每歲經費，即以餘銀七十萬兩生息，置田供支。

translations.literal: Annual expenses were to be met by investing the remaining seven hundred thousand taels at interest and purchasing land for support.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining seven hundred thousand taels would be invested and used to buy land whose rents would cover yearly upkeep.

sentences.zh: 上以津貼病民，撥部帑銀百萬。

translations.literal: The emperor held that the surcharge harmed the people and allocated one million taels from the ministry treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the surcharge as burdensome and allotted one million taels from central funds instead.

sentences.zh: 翰林院侍讀學士王炳瀛奏：「四川前買義田，遍​​及百餘州縣，若更以數十萬帑銀於各州縣買田收租，膏腴將盡歸公產。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academy attendant reader Wang Bingying memorialized: 'Sichuan has previously bought charitable fields spread across more than a hundred prefectures and counties; if hundreds of thousands more in treasury silver were used to buy land and collect rent in every prefecture and county, fertile land would nearly all become public property.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin reader Wang Bingying warned: "Sichuan already held charitable estates in over a hundred jurisdictions; spending hundreds of thousands more taels to buy land province-wide would turn most fertile soil into government holdings.

sentences.zh: 請限於四廳近邊地收買，安置屯防。」

translations.literal: He requested limiting purchases to land near the four subprefectures on the frontier and settling garrison colonists there.'
translations.idiomatic: He asked that purchases be confined to land near the four frontier subprefectures for garrison settlement."

sentences.zh: 下寶興妥議，疏言：「邊防完竣，用銀二十二萬兩有奇，以三十七萬發鹽茶各商，歲得息三萬七千餘兩，足敷增設練勇餉械之需。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to Baoxing for proper deliberation. He memorialized: 'Border defense completed will cost a little over 220,000 taels; lend 370,000 to salt and tea merchants, yielding over 37,000 taels interest yearly, sufficient for the pay and arms of added militia.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing was told to work out the details. He reported: "Finishing the frontier works would take just over 220,000 taels; lending 370,000 to salt and tea merchants would yield 37,000 taels a year—enough for the new militia's pay and equipment.

sentences.zh: 餘銀四十萬，聽部撥別用。」

translations.literal: The remaining 400,000 taels were left to the ministry to allocate elsewhere.'
translations.idiomatic: The remaining 400,000 taels would revert to the ministry for other uses."

sentences.zh: 遂罷買田議，二十一年，拜文淵閣大學士，留四川總督任。

translations.literal: The land-purchase plan was then abandoned. In the twenty-first year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory while retaining the Sichuan governor-generalship.
translations.idiomatic: The land-purchase scheme was dropped. In Daoguang 21 (1841) he became a Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory while remaining governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時大學士琦善、協辦大學士伊里布相繼罷，在朝滿洲大臣鮮當上意，故有是授。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Secretary Qishan and Associate Grand Secretary Yilibu had been dismissed in succession; few Manchu ministers at court pleased the emperor, hence this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan and Yilibu had just been removed from office, and few Manchu ministers in Beijing still enjoyed the emperor's trust—hence Baoxing's elevation.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，入覲，命留京管理刑部，充上書房總師傅，兼翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he came to audience, was ordered to remain in the capital to administer the Ministry of Justice, appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study, and concurrently chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 26 (1846) he was summoned to court, kept in Beijing to head the Ministry of Justice, made chief tutor of the Upper Study, and named chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十八年元旦，加恩年老諸臣，加太保。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the twenty-eighth year, in extending grace to aged officials, he was given the honorary title Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year audience of Daoguang 28 (1848) he received the honorary rank of Grand Tutor among favors granted to senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 十月，卒，年七十二，諡文莊。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he died, aged seventy-two; his posthumous title was Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month at seventy-two and was posthumously titled Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 宗室敬徵，隸鑲白旗，肅親王永錫子。

translations.literal: Imperial clansman Jingzheng was registered in the Bordered White Banner, son of Prince Su Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansman Jingzheng belonged to the Bordered White Banner and was a son of Prince Su Yongxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年，封輔國公，授頭等侍衛，兼委散秩大臣、副都統。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 10 he was enfeoffed as Duke Who Assists the State, appointed first-class imperial bodyguard, and concurrently entrusted as minister without regular rank and lieutenant-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 10 (1805) he was made Duke Who Assists the State, given first-class imperial bodyguard rank, and also served as an extraordinary minister and lieutenant-general.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授內閣學士，兼鑾儀使，充總族長。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Grand Secretariat academician, concurrently director of the Imperial Procession, and made chief clan head.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 19 (1814) he became a Grand Secretariat academician, also directed the Imperial Procession, and served as chief clan head.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，失察宗室海康等習紅陽教，褫職，謫居盛京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he failed to detect imperial clansmen Haikang and others practicing the Hongyang sect; his office was stripped and he was banished to Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 22 (1817) he was dismissed for failing to detect clansmen including Haikang practicing the Hongyang sect and was exiled to Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 尋予四等侍衛，乾清門行走。

translations.literal: Soon he was given fourth-class imperial bodyguard and service at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as fourth-class imperial bodyguard with duty at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 道光初，累遷工部侍郎，授內務府大臣，調戶部。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang he was promoted in succession to vice minister of Works, appointed minister of the Imperial Household, and transferred to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign he rose to vice minister of Works, headed the Imperial Household, and was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 八年，偕尚書王鼎察治長蘆鹽務，奏定歸補帑課章程，詳王鼎傳。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Minister Wang Ding, he investigated Changlu salt affairs and memorialized regulations for restoring treasury salt levies; details are in Wang Ding's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 8 (1828) he and Wang Ding investigated Changlu salt administration and framed rules for repaying arrears to the treasury; see Wang Ding's biography.

sentences.zh: 十二年，南河奸民陳堂等盜決於家灣官堤，命偕尚書硃士彥往勘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, ruffians of the Southern Rivers such as Chen Tang illicitly breached the official dike at Yujiawan; he was ordered together with Minister Zhu Shiyan to go and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 12 (1832), when ruffians led by Chen Tang cut the official dike at Yujiawan on the Southern Rivers, he was sent with Zhu Shiyan to inspect the damage.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「諸口已合，壩下尚未閉氣，間有蟄陷。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: 'The breaches have been closed, but below the dam the embankment has not yet fully settled and there are occasional sinkholes.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "The breaks were sealed but the foot of the dam had not fully compacted and sinkholes still appeared.

sentences.zh: 陳堂等聽從逸犯陳端糾眾，以為從例問擬，疏防各官遣戍。

translations.literal: Chen Tang and others followed the escaped convict Chen Duan in gathering a mob; they were sentenced under the statute for followers; officials negligent in defense were sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tang's gang had followed the fugitive Chen Duan; as accomplices they received reduced sentences, while negligent officials were banished.

sentences.zh: 通判張懋祖賠修壩工不實，罰賠枷號。

translations.literal: Subprefect Zhang Maozu's compensation for dike repairs was found false; he was fined, made to pay compensation, and placed in the cangue.
translations.idiomatic: Subprefect Zhang Maozu had falsified his dike-repair accounts and was fined, ordered to make restitution, and put in the cangue.

sentences.zh: 覆勘湖河各工，請擇要興修，高堰、山盱卑矮石工，分年改砌碎石；

translations.literal: On re-inspection of lake and river works he requested selective urgent repairs; the low stone works at Gaoyan and Shanyu were to be rebuilt with rubble stone over several years;
translations.idiomatic: Re-inspecting lake and river projects, he urged repairs where most needed—the low stone revetments at Gaoyan and Shanyu to be rebuilt in rubble over several years;

sentences.zh: 信壩補還石工，智壩、仁河、義河壩改修石底；

translations.literal: restore stone work at Xin Dam; rebuild the stone foundations of Zhi Dam and the Renhe and Yihe dams;
translations.idiomatic: restore stonework at Xin Dam; rebuild the stone foundations at Zhi Dam and the Renhe and Yihe barrages;

sentences.zh: 里河福興閘塌卸，急築；

translations.literal: the Fuxing Sluice on the inner river had collapsed and must be urgently rebuilt;
translations.idiomatic: the collapsed Fuxing Sluice on the inner canal needed urgent rebuilding;

sentences.zh: 揚河西岸加高磚工，改拋碎石。」

translations.literal: raise the brick revetment on the west bank of the Yangzhou River and change to dumped rubble stone.'
translations.idiomatic: raise the brick facing on the Yangzhou River's west bank and replace it with dumped rubble."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: The court approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved everything.

sentences.zh: 又會同兩江總督陶澍議定淮鹽票引兼行，言官所論官票運私、侵礙暢岸、爭佔馬頭三者皆可無慮，詔如原議行。

translations.literal: He also joined Governor-General Tao Shu of the Two Jiangs in fixing joint operation of Huai salt tickets and transport permits; the three points censors raised—official tickets used for private salt, encroachment on free-sale zones, and seizure of wharves—were all held groundless, and an edict ordered the original plan carried out.
translations.idiomatic: With Tao Shu, governor-general of the Two Jiangs, he finalized the combined ticket-and-permit system for Huai salt. Memorialists' fears—that official tickets would smuggle private salt, squeeze licensed markets, or monopolize wharves—were dismissed, and the original scheme was approved.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 14 (1834) he was made left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 偕侍郎吳椿勘浙江海塘，疏言：「念裡亭至尖山柴工尚資禦溜，石塘仍當修整，鎮海及戴家橋汛議改竹簍，塊石不如條石坦水舊法為堅實。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Minister Wu Chun he inspected the Zhejiang seawall and memorialized: 'From Nianli Pavilion to Jianshan, fascine works still help resist current; stone dikes should still be repaired. At Zhenhai and Daijiaqiao the plan to change to bamboo baskets is discussed; block stone is not as solid as the old method of strip stone on a level apron.
translations.idiomatic: With Vice Minister Wu Chun he surveyed Zhejiang's seawalls and reported: "Fascine works from Nianli Pavilion to Jianshan still helped break the surf and stone dikes needed repair; proposed bamboo baskets at Zhenhai and Daijiaqiao were inferior to the older strip-stone apron method.

sentences.zh: 烏龍廟以東，冬工暫緩。」

translations.literal: East of Wulong Temple, winter works were temporarily deferred.'
translations.idiomatic: Winter construction east of Wulong Temple could wait."

sentences.zh: 回京，擢兵部尚書，調工部。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he was promoted to minister of War and transferred to Works.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Beijing he was promoted to minister of War, then transferred to Works.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以孝穆皇后、孝慎皇后梓宮奉安龍泉峪，諏日不慎，罷尚書、都統，仍充內務府大臣。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, because the date chosen for installing the coffins of Empress Xiaomu and Empress Xiaoshen at Longquan Valley was ill considered, he was dismissed as minister and banner general but retained as minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 15 (1835), after an ill-chosen date for entombing Empresses Xiaomu and Xiaoshen at Longquan Valley, he lost his posts as minister and banner commander but kept his Imperial Household portfolio.

sentences.zh: 十六年，署戶部侍郎，累遷工部尚書，兼都統。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he acted as vice minister of Revenue, was promoted in succession to minister of Works, and concurrently served as banner general.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 16 (1836) he acted as vice minister of Revenue, then rose to minister of Works while also commanding a banner.

sentences.zh: 東河總督栗毓美多用磚工，御史李蓴言其不便，命敬徵偕蓴往勘。

translations.literal: Eastern Rivers Governor-General Li Yumei used brick works extensively; Censor Li Chun said this was impractical; Jingzheng was ordered to go with Li Chun to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Rivers governor Li Yumei favored brick revetments, Censor Li Chun objected, and Jingzheng was sent with Li Chun to inspect.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「已辦磚工尚屬整齊，輿論謂保灘護崖可資其力。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'Completed brick works are still in good order; public opinion holds that protecting beaches and banks can rely on their strength.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Existing brickworks were still sound and local opinion held they were useful for protecting banks and cliffs.

sentences.zh: 水深溜急之處，不及埽工鞏固，搶辦險工，未可深恃。

translations.literal: Where water is deep and current swift, they are less secure than fascine works; emergency repairs at dangerous points cannot be deeply relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: In deep, fast water they were less reliable than fascine revetments, and emergency repairs at danger spots could not be relied on indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 請停止燒磚，改辦碎石。」

translations.literal: He requested stopping brick firing and switching to rubble stone works.'
translations.idiomatic: He recommended halting new brick kilns and using rubble stone instead."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 十八年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 18 (1838) he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，南河揚河漫口，水由灌河入海。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the Yangzhou River of the Southern Rivers breached its banks and the water entered the sea by the Guan River.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 22 (1842) the Yangzhou River on the Southern Rivers overflowed and the current poured to sea through the Guan River.

sentences.zh: 有議即改新河，河督麟慶以河流未定，遽難決議，命敬徵偕尚書廖鴻荃往勘。

translations.literal: Some proposed immediately shifting to a new river course; River Governor Lin Qing held that the stream was still unsettled and a hasty decision was difficult; Jingzheng was ordered together with Minister Liao Hongquan to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged an immediate course change, but River Governor Lin Qing argued the stream was still unstable; Jingzheng was dispatched with Liao Hongquan to survey the scene.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「改河之議，在因勢利導。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'The proposal to change the river course lies in guiding according to the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized: "Redirecting the river meant working with the terrain, not against it.

sentences.zh: 今查灌河海口至蕭莊口門三百六十餘裡。

translations.literal: Now investigation shows from the Guan River estuary to the Xiaozhuang mouth is more than 360 li.
translations.idiomatic: From the Guan estuary to the Xiaozhuang outlet they measured more than 360 li.

sentences.zh: 新河正溜，由六塘出達灌口，其下游東北一百十里，滔滔直注。

translations.literal: The new river's main current exits through Liutang to reach the Guan mouth; downstream to the northeast for 110 li it pours straight on.
translations.idiomatic: The new main channel ran from Liutang to the Guan mouth, then northeast for 110 li in a straight, roaring torrent.

sentences.zh: 惟當潮漲時，黃水相逼，壅閼不前，而上游自口門至響水口二百餘裡，支流忽分忽合，必須兩岸築堤束水，方免汎濫。

translations.literal: Only at high tide does Yellow River water press in and block progress; upstream from the mouth to Xiangshui for more than 200 li, branch streams suddenly divide and reunite—dikes must be built on both banks to confine the water and prevent flooding.
translations.idiomatic: At high tide Yellow River water backed up and stalled the flow; upstream, over 200 li from the mouth to Xiangshui, channels split and rejoined unpredictably—only twin dikes could confine the water and prevent floods.

sentences.zh: 計工長三百餘裡，經費難籌。

translations.literal: The works would total more than 300 li in length and funds would be hard to raise.
translations.idiomatic: Dikes along 300-plus li would be prohibitively expensive.

sentences.zh: 且中河運道為黃流橫截，不得不移塘灌運。

translations.literal: Moreover the Grand Canal transport route in the middle river section is cut by Yellow River current and transport must be shifted to Liutang and the Guan route.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Canal trunk was cut by Yellow River water, forcing grain transport onto the Liutang–Guan detour.

sentences.zh: 清水本弱，仍恃借黃以濟。

translations.literal: Clear water is inherently weak and still relies on borrowing Yellow River water to assist.
translations.idiomatic: The clear-water section was already weak and still depended on Yellow River water to keep moving.

sentences.zh: 空船引轉需時，重運更形艱滯。

translations.literal: Empty boats require time to be towed and turned; laden transport becomes even more difficult and slow.
translations.idiomatic: Empty barges took longer to turn; laden grain convoys would fare even worse.

sentences.zh: 是移塘乃權宜之計，常年行之，恐妨運道。

translations.literal: Thus shifting to Liutang is an expedient; if carried out year after year, it may harm the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: The Liutang detour was a temporary fix; making it permanent would likely cripple the canal.

sentences.zh: 舊黃河自蕭莊迄舊海口四百二十餘裡，尾閭寬暢。

translations.literal: The old Yellow River from Xiaozhuang to the old estuary is more than 420 li, with a broad, open outlet.
translations.idiomatic: The old Yellow River course from Xiaozhuang to the former mouth ran 420-plus li with a wide, open outlet.

sentences.zh: 自漫口斷流，河身益淤。

translations.literal: Since the breach cut the flow, the riverbed has silted still more.
translations.idiomatic: Since the breach cut off the flow, the old channel had silted even further.

sentences.zh: 若挽歸故道，堵口挑河，共費五六百萬，較改河築堤撙節實多。

translations.literal: If the current were returned to the old course, blocking the mouth and dredging the river would cost five or six million altogether—far more economical than changing course and building dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Returning the river to its old bed—sealing the breach and dredging—would cost five or six million taels but still save far more than building new dikes on the Guan route.

sentences.zh: 請定明歲春融興工，俟軍船回空後築壩合龍。」

translations.literal: He requested fixing work to begin when ice melts next spring, and after grain transports return empty, building the closure dam and joining the channel.'
translations.idiomatic: He proposed starting when the ice broke the following spring and closing the breach after the grain fleet had returned empty."

sentences.zh: 詔如議行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the plan carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 尋以戶部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Associate Grand Secretary while minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Associate Grand Secretary while retaining the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，偕侍郎何汝霖赴南河勘工，又赴河南察視中河廳漫口。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, together with Vice Minister He Rulin he went to the Southern Rivers to inspect works, and again to Henan to examine the breach at the Middle River office.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 23 (1843) he and Vice Minister He Rulin inspected Southern Rivers projects, then surveyed the Middle River breach in Henan.

sentences.zh: 疏陳築壩挑河工費需銀五百十八萬兩，較祥符工費為節省，允之。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated that building the closure dam and dredging the river would require 5,180,000 taels of silver, more economical than the Xiangfu project costs; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that sealing the breach and dredging would cost 5.18 million taels—less than the Xiangfu works—and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，奏：「河南下北河廳廟工，乃北岸七廳適中之所，河臣宜常年駐此，便於控制。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he memorialized: 'The Miaogong works of the Lower North River office in Henan are midway among the seven offices on the north bank; the river governor should station here year-round for control.'
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 25 (1845) he proposed: "The Henan river governor should keep his headquarters at Miaogong, centrally placed among the seven north-bank offices."

sentences.zh: 詔河督每於伏汛前移駐廟工，立冬後仍回濟寧。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the river governor to move to Miaogong before the summer flood season each year and return to Jining after the Start of Winter.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered river governors to camp at Miaogong before the summer floods and return to Jining after winter.

sentences.zh: 尋坐濫保駐藏大臣孟保，降內閣學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was punished for indiscriminately recommending the Tibet resident minister Mengbao and was demoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon demoted to Grand Secretariat academician for improperly recommending Tibet resident minister Mengbao.

sentences.zh: 未幾，复授工部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was restored as minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 又坐濫保科布多參贊大臣果勒明阿，褫職。

translations.literal: He was again punished for indiscriminately recommending Kobdo expedition commissioner Guoleming'a and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his post again for improperly recommending Kobdo commissioner Guoleming'a.

sentences.zh: 三十年，署正白旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he served as acting lieutenant-general of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 30 (1850) he acted as lieutenant-general of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，卒，詔念前勞，予一品銜，依尚書例賜卹，諡文愨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he died; an edict recalled his earlier service, granted him first-rank insignia, burial benefits according to ministerial precedent, and the posthumous title Wenque.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianfeng 1 (1851); the court honored his past service with first-rank insignia, ministerial burial rites, and the posthumous title Wenque.

sentences.zh: 子恆恩，左副都御史；

translations.literal: His son Heng'en was left vice censor-in-chief;
translations.idiomatic: His son Heng'en became left vice censor-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 孫盛昱，自有傳。

translations.literal: his grandson Sheng Yu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: his grandson Sheng Yu is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 宗室禧恩，字仲蕃，隸正藍旗，睿親王淳穎子。

translations.literal: Imperial clansman Xi'en, style name Zhongfan, was registered in the Plain Blue Banner, son of Prince Rui Chunying.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansman Xi'en (style name Zhongfan) belonged to the Plain Blue Banner and was a son of Prince Rui Chunying.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年，賜頭品頂戴，授頭等侍衛，乾清門行走。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 6 he was granted first-rank insignia, appointed first-class imperial bodyguard, and served at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 6 (1801) he received first-rank insignia, became a first-class imperial bodyguard, and served at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 十年，晉御前侍衛，兼副都統、鑾儀使、上駟院卿，轉奉宸院卿，遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to imperial guard before the throne, concurrently lieutenant-general, director of the Imperial Procession, and master of the Imperial Stud, then transferred to director of the Imperial Parks, and promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 10 (1805) he rose to imperial guard before the throne, also commanding a banner, directing the Imperial Procession, and heading the Imperial Stud, then the Imperial Parks, and finally the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢理籓院侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to vice president of the Lifan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 18 (1813) he became vice president of the Lifan Court.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授內務府大臣，調戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed minister of the Imperial Household and transferred to vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 20 (1815) he headed the Imperial Household, then moved to vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，仁宗崩於熱河避暑山莊，事出倉猝，禧恩以內廷扈從，建議宣宗有定亂勳，當繼位。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Jiaqing Emperor died at the Rehe summer resort; the affair was sudden. Xi'en, attending within the palace, urged that the Daoguang Emperor, for his merit in quelling disorder, should succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiaqing Emperor died suddenly at Rehe in 1820, Xi'en—present in the inner court—argued that the Daoguang Emperor, who had merit in quelling disorder, should succeed.

sentences.zh: 樞臣托津、戴均元等猶豫，禧恩抗論，眾不能奪。

translations.literal: Grand councillors Tuojin, Dai Junyuan, and others hesitated; Xi'en argued forcefully and they could not prevail against him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand councillors Tuojin and Dai Junyuan wavered, but Xi'en's insistence carried the day.

sentences.zh: 會得秘匱硃諭，乃偕諸臣奉宣宗即位，命在御前大臣、領侍衛大臣上行走。

translations.literal: When a secret casket with vermilion rescript was obtained, he together with the other ministers installed the Daoguang Emperor; he was ordered to walk above the ranks of imperial guard grand ministers and chief guard grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Once the sealed succession edict appeared, he helped install the Daoguang Emperor and was ranked above the chief palace guards.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，擢理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: In Daoguang 2 he was promoted to minister of the Lifan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 (1822) he became minister of the Lifan Court.

sentences.zh: 時哈薩克部眾潛聚烏梁海，議遷徙安置，增設卡倫。

translations.literal: At the time Kazakh tribesmen were secretly gathering at Ulianghai; it was proposed to relocate and settle them and add guard posts.
translations.idiomatic: Kazakh groups were gathering covertly at Ulianghai; the court debated resettlement and new guard posts.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書松筠諳習邊事，上每垂詢，禧恩因以諮之。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Songyun was versed in frontier affairs; whenever the emperor inquired, Xi'en consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Minister Songyun knew frontier affairs, Xi'en consulted him whenever the emperor asked.

sentences.zh: 松筠素坦率，遂代刪改疏稿。

translations.literal: Songyun was naturally frank and forthright and so revised Xi'en's memorial draft.
translations.idiomatic: The outspoken Songyun took it upon himself to edit Xi'en's memorial.

sentences.zh: 禧恩怒，以上聞，松筠坐越職干預被譴。

translations.literal: Xi'en was angry and reported it to the emperor; Songyun was rebuked for overstepping his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Xi'en complained to the throne; Songyun was punished for meddling beyond his office.

sentences.zh: 尋調工部，仍兼署理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Works while still acting as minister of the Lifan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He soon moved to the Ministry of Works while continuing to act for the Lifan Court.

sentences.zh: 六年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 6 (1826) he transferred to Revenue.

sentences.zh: 八年，加太子少保，署吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and acted as minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 8 (1828) he received the Junior Guardian rank and acted as minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 九年，隨扈盛京，詔念睿親王多爾袞數定大勳，加恩後裔，賜禧恩雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, accompanying the emperor to Shengjing, an edict recalled Prince Rui Dorgon's great merit in establishing the dynasty and extended grace to his descendants, granting Xi'en double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: On the Shengjing tour in Daoguang 9 (1829), the court honored Dorgon's service and granted Xi'en double peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 十二年，湖南江華瑤趙金龍作亂，命禧恩偕盛京將軍瑚松額督師，未至，總督盧坤、提督羅思舉已平之，殲金龍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Yao Zhao Jinlong rebelled in Jianghua, Hunan; Xi'en was ordered with Shengjing General Husong'e to command troops. Before they arrived, Governor Lu Kun and Provincial Commander Luo Siju had already pacified the rebellion and killed Jinlong.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 12 (1832), when the Yao leader Zhao Jinlong rose in Jianghua, Xi'en was sent with General Husong'e—but Lu Kun and Luo Siju had already crushed the revolt and killed Jinlong before they arrived.

sentences.zh: 禧恩素貴倨，奉命視師，意氣甚盛，嗛諸將不待而告捷，謂金龍死未可信。

translations.literal: Xi'en had always been proud of his rank; ordered to inspect the army, he was in high spirits and resented that the generals reported victory without waiting for him, saying Jinlong's death could not be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Accustomed to privilege, Xi'en marched in high style and refused to believe the victory reports, insisting Jinlong might still be alive.

sentences.zh: 思舉以金龍焚骸及佩物為證，議始息。

translations.literal: Siju produced Jinlong's burned remains and personal effects as proof, and the dispute ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Siju produced Jinlong's charred body and belongings, ending the argument.

sentences.zh: 廣東瑤匪趙仔青竄入湖南，率提督餘步雲、總兵曾勝追剿之；

translations.literal: The Yao bandit Zhao Zaiqing from Guangdong fled into Hunan; he led Provincial Commander Yu Buyun and Regional Commander Zeng Sheng in pursuit;
translations.idiomatic: When the Guangdong Yao rebel Zhao Zaiqing fled into Hunan, he led Yu Buyun and Zeng Sheng in pursuit;

sentences.zh: 偕巡撫吳榮光疏陳善後事。

translations.literal: together with Governor Wu Rongguang he memorialized on pacification measures.
translations.idiomatic: and with Governor Wu Rongguang memorialized on postwar arrangements.

sentences.zh: 湖南既定，而兩廣總督李鴻賓剿連山瑤，閱半年，軍屢挫。

translations.literal: Hunan was settled, but Governor-General Li Hongbin of the Two Guangs was suppressing the Lianshan Yao and for half a year the army suffered repeated setbacks.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan was quiet, but in Guangdong Li Hongbin's campaign against the Lianshan Yao stalled for six months.

sentences.zh: 詔逮鴻賓，以禧恩署總督，由湖南進兵。

translations.literal: An edict arrested Hongbin and had Xi'en act as governor-general, advancing from Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongbin was arrested and Xi'en took over as acting governor-general, advancing from Hunan.

sentences.zh: 遣步雲、勝等先後破賊，擒首逆鄧三、盤文理，毀其巢。

translations.literal: He sent Buyun, Sheng, and others in succession to defeat the bandits, capture the ringleaders Deng San and Pan Wenli, and destroy their lairs.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Buyun and Sheng to rout the rebels, capture leaders Deng San and Pan Wenli, and destroy their strongholds.

sentences.zh: 甫一月，諸瑤乞降。

translations.literal: Within a month all the Yao submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the Yao surrendered.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其奏功迅速，賜三眼花翎，封不入八分輔國公。

translations.literal: An edict praised his swift success, granted triple peacock feathers, and enfeoffed him as Duke Who Assists the State not entered in the eight grades.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his speed, gave him triple peacock feathers, and made him Duke Who Assists the State outside the eight grades.

sentences.zh: 班師，途次丁母憂，溫諭慰之。

translations.literal: Returning from campaign he was midway in mourning for his mother; a warm edict consoled him.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home he entered mourning for his mother; the emperor sent condolences.

sentences.zh: 十三年，孝慎皇后薨，命理喪儀，坐議禮徵引違制，褫御前大臣、戶部尚書、內務府大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when Empress Xiaoshen died, he was charged with funeral rites but was stripped of his posts as imperial guard grand minister, minister of Revenue, and minister of the Imperial Household for citing ritual precedents in violation of regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 13 (1833), while arranging Empress Xiaoshen's funeral, he lost his guard, Revenue, and Imperial Household posts for improper ritual citations.

sentences.zh: 尋复授理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed minister of the Lifan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as Lifan minister.

sentences.zh: 以生日受屬員饋送，為御史趙敦詩所劾，疏辯得直，敦詩坐譴。

translations.literal: For accepting gifts from subordinates on his birthday he was impeached by Censor Zhao Dunshi; he memorialized in defense and was upheld; Dunshi was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhao Dunshi accused him of taking birthday gifts from subordinates; Xi'en's defense prevailed and Zhao was punished.

sentences.zh: 十四年，因相度龍泉峪萬年吉地，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, for surveying the eternal resting place at Longquan Valley, he was given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 14 (1834), for surveying the imperial tomb site at Longquan Valley, he received the Grand Guardian rank.

sentences.zh: 調兵部尚書，兼署禮部戶部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of War and concurrently acted for Rites and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of War while also acting for Rites and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十八年，詔以南苑牲畜不蕃，禧恩久管奉宸苑，廢弛疏懈，罷其兼領。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year an edict said livestock in the Southern Park were not multiplying; Xi'en had long managed the Imperial Parks and was negligent; his concurrent posts were removed.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 18 (1838) the emperor blamed him for declining herds in the Southern Park and stripped his concurrent offices.

sentences.zh: 尋得員司積弊狀，盡罷諸兼職，降內閣學士。

translations.literal: Soon evidence of accumulated abuses by clerks emerged and all his concurrent posts were abolished; he was demoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: Clerical corruption then came to light; he lost every concurrent post and dropped to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，署盛京將軍，授理籓院侍郎，留將軍署任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he acted as governor-general of Shengjing and was appointed vice president of the Lifan Court while retaining the Shengjing post.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 22 (1842) he acted as Shengjing governor-general and became Lifan vice president while keeping that command.

sentences.zh: 英吉利內犯，海疆戒嚴，命治盛京防務。

translations.literal: England invaded inland and the coast was on alert; he was ordered to organize Shengjing defenses.
translations.idiomatic: When the English invaded inland and the coast was on alert, he was ordered to prepare Shengjing's defenses.

sentences.zh: 既而和議成，疏陳善後十事，並巡洋章程，如議行。

translations.literal: After peace was made he memorialized ten pacification measures and regulations for coastal patrol, all approved.
translations.idiomatic: After the peace settlement he proposed ten coastal reforms and patrol rules, all adopted.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以病解職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 25 (1845) he retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 坐失察內地民人越朝鮮界墾地，削公爵，降二等輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was punished for failing to detect inland civilians crossing into Korea to reclaim land; his ducal title was revoked and he was reduced to second-rank Brigadier General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his dukedom for failing to stop Chinese settlers encroaching on Korean territory and was reduced to second-rank brigadier general.

sentences.zh: 三十年，起署馬蘭鎮總兵、密雲副都統。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was recalled to act as commanding general of Malan garrison and deputy lieutenant-general of Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 30 (1850) he returned as Malan garrison commander and Miyun deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，召授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was summoned as vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 1 (1851) he was recalled as vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢戶部尚書，協辦大學士，管理籓院事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to minister of Revenue, Associate Grand Secretary, and charged with Lifan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 (1852) he became Revenue minister, Associate Grand Secretary, and head of Lifan affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太子太保，諡文莊。

translations.literal: Soon he died; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died shortly after, posthumously made Grand Guardian with the title Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 禧恩自道光初被恩眷，及孝全皇后被選入宮，家故寒素，賴其資助，遂益用事。

translations.literal: From early Daoguang Xi'en enjoyed imperial favor; when Empress Xiaoquan was chosen for the palace, her family was poor and relied on his support, and his influence grew.
translations.idiomatic: Favored from early Daoguang, Xi'en backed the impecunious family of the future Empress Xiaoquan and grew still more powerful.

sentences.zh: 遍膺禁近要職，兼攝諸部，凌轢同列，人皆側目。

translations.literal: He held every key post near the throne and concurrently headed many ministries, overbearing toward colleagues until all looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: He monopolized palace posts and ministries alike, bullying peers until courtiers watched him with resentment.

sentences.zh: 後晚寵衰，禧恩亦數獲譴罷斥。

translations.literal: Later, as the empress's favor waned, Xi'en too was repeatedly punished and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress later fell from favor, Xi'en was punished and dismissed repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，乃復起，不兩年登協揆焉。

translations.literal: After the Xianfeng Emperor acceded, he was raised again and within two years reached the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xianfeng Emperor he was restored and reached the Grand Secretariat within two years.

sentences.zh: 陳官俊，字偉堂，山東濰縣人。

translations.literal: Chen Guanjun, style name Weitang, was a native of Weixian in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guanjun (style name Weitang) was from Weixian, Shandong.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷贊善。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 13 he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and promoted to mentor of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Jiaqing 13 (1808), entered the Hanlin, became a compiler, and rose to mentor of the heir.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，入直上書房。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he entered the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 21 (1816) he joined the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 大考二等，擢洗馬，累遷右庶子。

translations.literal: In the great examination he placed second class and was promoted to groom of the heir's stable, then in succession to right vice director of the Studies.
translations.idiomatic: After placing second class in the palace examination he became groom of the heir's stable and then right vice director of the Studies.

sentences.zh: 典陝西鄉試，督山西學政。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial examination and supervised Shanxi education.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the Shaanxi provincial exams and served as Shanxi education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，命各省明定陋規，中外臣工多言窒礙，官俊亦疏陳不可行，詔嘉之，予議敘。

translations.literal: In Daoguang 1 the throne ordered each province to define improper fees clearly; officials inside and outside the court mostly said it would obstruct administration, and Guanjun also memorialized that it was impracticable; an edict praised this and granted him consideration for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 (1821), when the court ordered provinces to abolish informal fees, most officials objected; Guanjun agreed and was commended and marked for promotion.

sentences.zh: 會密諭留心察訪官吏賢否、政治得失，官俊恃曾直內廷為宣宗所眷，意氣甚張。

translations.literal: When secret instructions came to watch officials' merit and policy failures, Guanjun, relying on his former service in the inner court and the Daoguang Emperor's favor, became very overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with secret orders to report on officials, he grew arrogant, trusting in his old intimacy with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍講學士，命回京，仍直上書房。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to attendant reader and ordered back to the capital, still on Upper Study duty.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made attendant reader, recalled to Beijing, and kept on Upper Study duty.

sentences.zh: 山西巡撫成格追劾官俊在學政任毆差買妾，妄作威福，大開奔競。

translations.literal: Shanxi Governor Cheng Ge pursued charges that while education commissioner Guanjun had beaten runners and bought a concubine, acting tyrannically and opening the door to favor-seeking.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi Governor Cheng Ge then accused him of beating runners, buying a concubine, and encouraging corruption while education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上以官俊於毆差買妾已自承不諱，曾薦舉魏元烺、邱鳴泰，人材尚不繆；

translations.literal: The emperor said Guanjun had already confessed to beating runners and buying a concubine, and that his recommendations of Wei Yuanlang and Qiu Mingtai showed his judgment of talent was not wholly wrong;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted Guanjun had confessed to the beating and concubine, and that his nominees Wei Yuanlang and Qiu Mingtai showed he could still judge talent;

sentences.zh: 惟所述太監往河東查訪鹽務控案，事出無稽，解職就質，命長齡道出山西，傳旨面詰成格，亦以不能指實引咎，遂兩斥之。

translations.literal: only the tale of eunuchs going to Hedong to investigate salt affairs was groundless; he was dismissed to answer charges; Changling was ordered via Shanxi to question Cheng Ge face to face, and as Cheng could not substantiate his claims he too was rebuked, and both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: but the story of eunuchs investigating salt at Hedong was fiction. Guanjun was dismissed to stand trial; Changling was sent to confront Cheng Ge, who could not prove his charges, and both men were removed.

sentences.zh: 官俊降編修，罷直上書房。

translations.literal: Guanjun was demoted to compiler and dismissed from the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: Guanjun was reduced to compiler and expelled from the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 連典貴州、江西鄉試，歷中允、祭酒、侍講學士、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He presided in succession over the Guizhou and Jiangxi provincial examinations and served as vice director of studies, libationer, attendant reader, and Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He later ran the Guizhou and Jiangxi exams and held posts from vice director of studies to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授禮部侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed vice minister of Rites and transferred to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 16 (1836) he became vice minister of Rites, then Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十九年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 19 (1839) he was made minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 東陵郎中慶玉侵帑籍沒，主事全孚預告，多所寄頓。

translations.literal: Langzhong Qingyu of the Eastern Tombs embezzled treasury funds and was confiscated; clerk Quan Fu had forewarned him and much was hidden away.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Tombs official Qingyu embezzled funds and was ruined, clerk Quan Fu had tipped him off and much property was hidden.

sentences.zh: 事覺，語由官俊閒談漏洩，回奏复諱飾，詔斥失大臣體，褫職。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light the story leaked through Guanjun's casual talk; in his reply he again concealed the facts; an edict rebuked him for lacking a minister's bearing and stripped his office.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread through Guanjun's loose talk; he then covered up in his memorial and was dismissed for unworthy conduct.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，起為通政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was recalled as commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 21 (1841) he returned as transmission commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部、吏部侍郎，管理三庫。

translations.literal: He served as vice minister of Revenue and Personnel and managed the three treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of Revenue and Personnel and managed the three treasuries.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部尚書，調工部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of Rites and transferred to Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of Rites, then Works.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he became Associate Grand Secretary while minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 24 (1844) he became Associate Grand Secretary while heading Personnel.

sentences.zh: 官俊再起，歷典鄉會試、殿廷禦試，每與衡校。

translations.literal: When Guanjun rose again he presided in turn over provincial, metropolitan, and palace examinations, taking part in grading each time.
translations.idiomatic: Restored to favor, he repeatedly chaired provincial, metropolitan, and palace examinations.

sentences.zh: 充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: He served as chief tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 編修童福承素無行，直上書房授皇子讀。

translations.literal: Compiler Tong Fucheng had always been of bad character yet taught princes in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Tong Fucheng, notoriously dissolute, still taught princes in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳壇劾之，語及福承為官俊妻作祭文，措詞過當。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Tan impeached him, mentioning that Fucheng had written a funeral elegy for Guanjun's wife with excessive wording.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Tan impeached him, citing an overwrought funeral elegy Tong had written for Guanjun's wife.

sentences.zh: 福承譴黜，詔斥官俊容隱不奏，罷總師傅，議降三級調用，從寬留任。

translations.literal: Fucheng was censured and dismissed; an edict rebuked Guanjun for concealing the matter and not reporting it, removed him as chief tutor, proposed demotion by three ranks and transfer, but leniently allowed him to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was dismissed; Guanjun was rebuked for shielding him, stripped of the chief tutorship, and spared demotion on leniency.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，卒，優詔賜卹，稱其心田坦白，贈太子太保，入祀賢良祠，諡文愨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died; a favorable edict granted burial benefits, calling his mind open and candid, posthumously giving Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, entry in the Temple of Worthies, and the posthumous title Wenque.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Daoguang 29 (1849) with generous rites, praised as frank-hearted, posthumously made Grand Guardian, enshrined among worthies, and titled Wenque.

sentences.zh: 賜其孫厚鍾、厚滋並為舉人。

translations.literal: His grandsons Houchong and Houzi were both granted juren status.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons Houchong and Houzi were both granted juren degrees.

sentences.zh: 官俊初直上書房，授宣宗長子奕緯讀，宣宗嘉其訓迪有方。

translations.literal: When Guanjun first served in the Upper Study he taught the Daoguang Emperor's eldest son Yiwei; the emperor praised his instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He had tutored the Daoguang Emperor's eldest son Yiwei; the emperor praised his teaching.

sentences.zh: 後皇長子逾冠而薨，上深以為恫，故遇官俊特厚，屢獲咎而恩禮始終不衰。

translations.literal: Later the eldest imperial son passed the capping age and died; the emperor was deeply grieved, and therefore treated Guanjun with special favor, repeatedly punishing yet never withdrawing grace.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince died young, the grieving emperor favored Guanjun throughout, pardoning repeated faults.

sentences.zh: 子介祺，道光二十五年進士，官編修。

translations.literal: His son Jieqi, jinshi of Daoguang 25, served as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jieqi, a Daoguang 25 jinshi, became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，助軍餉，加侍講學士銜。

translations.literal: During Xianfeng he aided military funds and was given the rank of attendant reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianfeng era he contributed to military funds and received attendant reader rank.

sentences.zh: 後在籍治團練，守城，賑饑，賜二品頂戴。

translations.literal: Later at home he organized militia, defended the city, and relieved famine; he was granted second-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: At home he raised militia, defended the city, and ran famine relief, earning second-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 介祺績學好古，所藏鐘鼎、彝器、金石為近代之冠。

translations.literal: Jieqi was learned and fond of antiquity; his collection of bells, tripods, bronzes, and stone inscriptions was the finest of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Jieqi was a scholar-collector whose bronzes and epigraphy ranked among the finest of his day.

sentences.zh: 卓秉恬，字靜遠，四川華陽人。

translations.literal: Zhuo Bingtian, style name Jingyuan, was a native of Huayang in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Bingtian (style name Jingyuan) was from Huayang, Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年進士，選庶吉士，年甫逾冠，授檢討。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 7 he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as Hanlin bachelor; barely past twenty, he was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Jiaqing 7 (1802), entered the Hanlin at barely twenty, and became a reviser.

sentences.zh: 典陝西鄉試。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the Shaanxi provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 十八年，改御史，歷給事中，章疏凡數十上。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to censor, served in succession as supervising secretary, and submitted several dozen memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 18 (1813) he became a censor, then supervising secretary, filing dozens of memorials.

sentences.zh: 論盜風未息，由捕役與盜賊因緣為奸，捕役藉盜賊以漁利，盜賊仗捕役為護符，民間控告，官不為理，盜賊結恨，又召荼毒；

translations.literal: He argued that banditry had not ceased because constables colluded with thieves—constables profited through thieves, thieves relied on constables as talismans, when commoners sued officials would not act, and thieves nursed hatred and brought further calamity;
translations.idiomatic: He argued banditry persisted because constables and thieves colluded—constables profited, thieves enjoyed protection, lawsuits went nowhere, and victims were punished again;

sentences.zh: 直隸之大名、滄州，河南之衛輝、陳州、山東之曹州、東昌、武定，江甦之徐州最甚，請飭實力禁懲。

translations.literal: it was worst in Daming and Cangzhou in Zhili, Weihui and Chenzhou in Henan, Caozhou, Dongchang, and Wuding in Shandong, and Xuzhou in Jiangsu; he requested strict prohibition and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: worst in Daming, Cangzhou, Weihui, Chenzhou, Caozhou, Dongchang, Wuding, and Xuzhou; he demanded stern enforcement.

sentences.zh: 巡漕山東，履勘泰安、兗州各屬，探濬新泉四十三處，定名勒石。

translations.literal: While inspecting the Grand Canal in Shandong he traveled through Tai'an and Yanzhou subordinates, opened forty-three new springs, and set names carved in stone.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting the Shandong canal he surveyed Tai'an and Yanzhou, opened forty-three springs, and recorded their names on stone.

sentences.zh: 歷鴻臚寺少卿、順天府丞。

translations.literal: He served in succession as vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and vice prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and vice prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，疏言：「由陝西略陽迄東至湖北鄖西，謂之南山老林；

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he memorialized: 'From Lueyang in Shaanxi eastward to Yunxi in Hubei is called the Old Forest of the Southern Mountains;
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 25 (1820) he memorialized: "From Lueyang in Shaanxi east to Yunxi in Hubei lay the Southern Mountains Old Forest;

sentences.zh: 由陝西寧羌迄南而東，經四川境至湖北保康，謂之巴山老林。

translations.literal: from Ningqiang in Shaanxi south and east through Sichuan to Baokang in Hubei is called the Old Forest of the Ba Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: from Ningqiang south and east through Sichuan to Baokang in Hubei lay the Ba Mountains Old Forest.

sentences.zh: 地皆磽瘠，糧徭極微。

translations.literal: The land is all barren and poor; grain levies and corvée are extremely light.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was poor and taxes light.

sentences.zh: 無業遊民，給地主錢數千，即租種數溝數嶺。

translations.literal: Idle wanderers gave landlords several thousand cash and at once rented several ravines and hillsides.
translations.idiomatic: Jobless migrants paid landlords a few thousand cash to farm scattered ravines and hillsides.

sentences.zh: 歲薄不收則徙去，謂之棚民。

translations.literal: If the year was poor and there was no harvest they moved away; they were called shed people.
translations.idiomatic: They moved on after bad harvests and were known as shed dwellers.

sentences.zh: 良莠莫辨，攘奪時聞。

translations.literal: Good and bad could not be distinguished; plunder was often heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Good and bad mixed together, and robbery was common.

sentences.zh: 一遇旱澇，一二奸民為之倡，即蟻附蜂起。

translations.literal: Whenever drought or flood occurred, one or two wicked commoners took the lead and people swarmed like ants and bees.
translations.idiomatic: Drought or flood could set a few agitators off and crowds would rise like swarming insects.

sentences.zh: 州縣以地方遼闊，莫能追捕，遂至互相容隱。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties, because the territory was vast, could not pursue and arrest, and so came to conceal one another's failures.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials, unable to police such vast terrain, covered for one another.

sentences.zh: 迨釀成大案，即加參劾，事已無濟。

translations.literal: Only when a major case had formed would they be impeached, by which time nothing could be done.
translations.idiomatic: Impeachment came only after full-blown outbreaks, when it was too late.

sentences.zh: 且事連三省，大吏往返諮商，州縣奉文辦理，恆在數月之後。

translations.literal: Moreover the affair involved three provinces; high officials went back and forth in consultation, and when prefectures and counties received documents to act, it was always months later.
translations.idiomatic: Cases spanned three provinces; provincial leaders took months to coordinate, and local orders arrived still later.

sentences.zh: 與其即一隅而專謀之，何如合三省而共議之。

translations.literal: Rather than planning for one corner alone, how much better to join the three provinces in common deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Better to govern the region jointly than to treat each corner separately.

sentences.zh: 請於扼要之地，專設大員控制。」

translations.literal: He requested that at strategic points a dedicated high official be appointed for control.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed posting senior officials at key points to supervise the area."

sentences.zh: 宣宗深韙之，詔下三省會議，未果行，僅將邊境文武酌就要地改駐添設。

translations.literal: The Daoguang Emperor deeply approved; an edict was sent for the three provinces to confer, but it was not carried out—only border civil and military officials were redeployed or added at selected points.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoguang Emperor approved, but interprovincial talks came to nothing; only a few border posts were reinforced or relocated.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，調奉天府丞，丁父憂去。

translations.literal: In Daoguang 4 he was transferred to vice prefect of Fengtian and left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 4 (1824) he was transferred to vice prefect of Fengtian, then left for mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，歷太僕寺、大理寺少卿，太僕寺卿，宗人府丞，內閣學士，典江南鄉試。

translations.literal: After mourning he served in succession as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, vice president of the Court of Judicial Review, minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, Grand Secretariat academician, and presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he rose through the Stud and Judicial Review courts, the Clan Court, the Grand Secretariat, and chaired the Jiangnan provincial exams.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷禮部侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to vice minister of Rites and transferred to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 15 (1835) he became vice minister of Rites, then Personnel.

sentences.zh: 督浙江學政。

translations.literal: He supervised Zhejiang education.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Zhejiang education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 擢左都御史，召還京，兼管順天府尹事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left censor-in-chief, recalled to the capital, and concurrently managed the Shuntian prefect's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to left censor-in-chief, he returned to Beijing and also ran Shuntian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部、戶部、吏部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: He served in succession as minister of War, Revenue, and Personnel, and as Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He headed War, Revenue, and Personnel in turn and became Associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，拜文淵閣大學士，晉武英殿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Profundity and advanced to the Hall of Military Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 24 (1844) he entered the Grand Secretariat at the Hall of Literary Profundity and moved to the Hall of Military Eminence.

sentences.zh: 歷管兵部、戶部、工部，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He headed in succession the ministries of War, Revenue, and Works, and was granted peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw War, Revenue, and Works in turn and received peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，卒，年七十四，贈太子太保，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng he died, aged seventy-four; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianfeng 5 (1855) at seventy-four, posthumously made Grand Guardian with the title Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 秉恬兼管京尹最久，凡十有八年。

translations.literal: Bingtian concurrently managed the capital prefecture longest, altogether eighteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtian ran the capital prefecture longer than anyone—eighteen years in all.

sentences.zh: 時九卿會議，一二王公樞相主之，餘率佔位畫諾。

translations.literal: At the time in conferences of the nine ministers, one or two princes and grand councillors presided and the rest mostly filled seats and assented.
translations.idiomatic: At ministerial conferences a prince or grand councillor led while the rest rubber-stamped.

sentences.zh: 秉恬在列，時有辯論，不為用事者所喜。

translations.literal: Bingtian was present and sometimes argued; he was not liked by those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtian often spoke up in debate, which displeased the power holders.

sentences.zh: 子枟，道光二十年進士，官至吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Yun, jinshi of Daoguang 20, rose to vice minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun, a Daoguang 20 jinshi, became vice minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自設軍機處，閣臣不預樞務。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Since the Grand Council was established, Grand Secretariat ministers did not participate in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: After the Grand Council was created, Grand Secretariat ministers no longer handled core state secrets.

sentences.zh: 始猶取名德較著者表望中朝，繼則旅進旅退之流，且以年資眷睞，馴躋鼎鉉矣。

translations.literal: At first men of rather notable virtue and repute were still chosen to display prestige at court; later came those who advanced and retreated in groups, and by seniority and imperial favor gently reached the highest ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: At first the court still chose men of real standing; later mediocrities rose by seniority and favor to the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 寶興號嫺吏事，而蒙簠簋不飭之聲；

translations.literal: Baoxing was known as skilled in administrative affairs, yet bore the reputation of lax integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing was considered capable in administration yet suspected of loose integrity;

sentences.zh: 敬徵數視河工，差著勞勚；

translations.literal: Jingzheng repeatedly inspected river works and showed some merit in labor;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzheng earned some credit on repeated river inspections;

sentences.zh: 禧恩、陳官俊並恃恩私，崛而復起；

translations.literal: Xi'en and Chen Guanjun both relied on private favor, rising again after setbacks;
translations.idiomatic: Xi'en and Chen Guanjun both rode private favor back into power after falls;

sentences.zh: 卓秉恬以言官進，視緘默自安者稍表異焉。

translations.literal: Zhuo Bingtian advanced as a speaking official and showed himself slightly different from those who kept silent for safety.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Bingtian, who entered as a memorializing censor, stood somewhat apart from officials who kept quiet to stay safe.
